absent: Compatibility predicates for file-backed and anonymous mappings and their exclusions.
Internals of sharing teardown, bulk unmerge, stable teardown, node removal, offline waiting, and advisor default selection.
Layouts and additional locking for slot, scan cursor, reverse-mapping item, and stable node structures.
Numeric values and full transitions of run, offline, merge-any, and mergeable flags.
Concurrency and ordering guarantees for unsynchronized tunables and counters.
Allocation failure handling beyond immediate error return and daemon wakeup conditions beyond first entry.
Show-handler output details for prune interval, smart scan, advisor limits, and zero-page accounting beyond decimal emission.

findings.text: This lane exposes address-space merge management through a flags helper for new mappings, enable and disable helpers for whole spaces, a mode-aware disable entry, and a madvise handler for per-range control.
Enrollment lifecycle registers an address space on first use and unregisters on teardown, with allocation and reference handling on entry and fast versus deferred release on exit.
Query helpers report whether any mapping in a space carries the mergeable mark and estimate memory profit from merging after subtracting tracking overhead.

Eligibility rejects areas already marked mergeable and otherwise defers to a compatibility check; adding marks eligible areas, removal tears down sharing over the full extent when anonymous state exists then clears the mark, and madvise merge and unmerge follow the same allow and teardown pattern over the advised extent.

Whole-space enablement registers the space when needed, records the any-mode flag, then visits every mapping to mark eligibles; disablement visits to unmark with restoration on failure before clearing the flag; the new-mapping helper marks eligibles while any-mode is active and re-registers if the mergeable record was lost.

Registration reserves a slot, notes whether the global list was empty to decide on wakeup, links the entry relative to the scanner position according to unmerge mode, records mergeable state, retains the space, wakes the background thread only for the first entry, and emits an enter trace.

Exit resolves the slot under protection; missing entries and cursor-resident entries take no list action, entries without reverse-mapping state are detached and freed immediately with flags cleared and reference dropped, while entries with such state are repositioned near the cursor and synchronized through a paired write acquisition.

Pruning by frame interval discards entries whose stored frame lies inside the half-open range; singletons are handled directly, chains sweep duplicates safely and release the chain object when emptied to signal rebalancing, and the checker restarts from the first root after rebalancing while also sweeping a migration queue with periodic voluntary yields.
A dedicated spin guard protects the global slot registry and list plus cursor comparisons during registration and teardown.
A thread mutex combined with an offline wait serializes run control, cross-node reconfiguration, sharing-limit changes, and offline transitions.
Address-space exclusion requires write hold for whole-space disable, at least read hold for mergeable scans, and a paired write hold in the deferred exit path to synchronize with copy handling.

Run control accepts only bounded numeric selections, applies changes under exclusion, performs a full unmerge pass with origin marking when unmerge is requested and reverts to stopped on failure, and wakes the background thread when merging is requested.

Offline handling records an offline mark when going offline, prunes stable structures over the notified range on completed offline before clearing the mark and waking waiters, and clears with wakeup on cancellation.

Tunable stores validate before updating: sleep and chain-prune intervals accept decimal milliseconds, batch size is refused while automatic advice is active, boolean knobs accept truth spellings, advisor numeric limits accept unsigned values with the target requiring a positive value, and advisor mode accepts two named selections and refreshes defaults on change.

Cross-node and sharing-limit updates allow no-change writes, otherwise require idle sharing with successful stable teardown or report busy; the cross-node selection is binary and lazily provisions per-node roots while preserving existing unstable state, and the sharing selection demands at least double sharing with an optimistic precheck.

Status reads publish daemon counters in decimal; the volatile estimate is derived without locking and clamped at zero, while profit estimates combine sharing and zero savings scaled by page size minus tracking overhead.

Exposed controls are collected in a null-terminated pointer table under one group name, with cross-node control included only when multi-node support is configured, using read-only and read-write helper definitions.
The attribute group name presented to user space is ksm.
Advisor mode display brackets the active choice between none and scan-time, and stores accept those two spellings.
Boolean controls accept boolean spellings, numeric controls accept base-ten integers, and invalid spellings or out-of-range selections are rejected.

Volatile accounting without locking can transiently underflow and is clamped; offline pruning must exclude scanning and bulk removal while permitting fault and lookup paths; freeing at the scan cursor is deferred; insertion position during unmerge is required so fresh spaces are not missed.
The memory notifier always reports successful handling after processing offline transitions.
